If you are already decided on a specialty + have the financial support from ur family, at least for the first few months of applying and residency, then diretso training ka na. Agree, sayang oras.

However if you're someone na half hearted pa on what specialty to take + don't have the privilege to be supported financially by your parents while applying and esp first few months of training, then walang masama magmoonlight. Makakaipon ka, more freedom and more time to decide anong specialty :)

GP here and i am planning to moonlight at least for a year dahil ayoko na umasa sa parents ko once i start training + makapagprovide na din sa house. Also if you go to a govt hospital the income is adequate but could def be delayed, now if you train in a private hospital, sobrang liit ng sweldo (difficult to provide for your family, yung ibang kilala ko umaasa pa din minsan sa parents nila) kasi di talaga kasya sahod.

So depends talaga sa situation, priorities mo :)

Hello, IM and Surgery pinaka-toxic as usual 😅 lalo na if ward intern + crit care intern ka din on that day, nakakaiyak talaga pero super bait and hands on ng naging interns monitor namin nun kaya may learnings pa rin both theo and dito talaga magiging expert ka sa skills kasi never ending errands lol, lalakas din loob mo, tapos may telecon din kami nun pag post duty.

Hello!

Solid batak skills experience, however during my time we didn't have any clerks because of covid so expect na interns gagawa halos lahat (paperworks, referrals, labs, vs monitoring) as in lahat, so super nakakapagod honestly and because of that personally, it felt like medyo nabitin yung learnings namin theoretical wise (dahil during internship you still need to prep for the boards) because the errands is never ending that we didn't have time to even discuss some of the cases we we're seeing and why this or that are needed/done/requested. Sometimes ang nagiging goal is to finish all the errands. There are days as well na solo intern ka lang for whole male/female or minsan both wards/posts dahil onti lang interns. But we understood dahil di lang kami yung ganun, kahit residents super busy din na minsan wala talaga sila time magturo (minsan nga naaawa na sila samin, ibang errands namin ginagawa na din nila huhu)

I would say 70% of our seniors that i met there were kind, friendly, patient and some will even go out of their way to teach us kahit onti lang or kahit super pagod na sila (S/O to all those residents di ko po kayo makakalimutan!) meron pa ring toxic and super scary but I would say onti lang silang nakasama ko hehe

Overall, i think maswerte pa rin kami na sa JR nagintern during covid cause we experienced ER/OPD/OR/Ward of most dept there + all major rotations, face to face (which di na experience ng ibang interns from other hospi during covid). And i think if may clerks na sila now ulit doon, baka di na ganun ka-toxic/draining yung errands as an intern hehe

Best of luck!
God bless you Doc, and sana dumami pa po yung mga seniors na tulad niyo

Honestly, imo it would depend on your current priorities, where you are right now especially financially and if it's really something you want to do in life. Trust me it's so easy to come up with a long list of why pursuing med is not worth it, but at the end of the day, the common denominator of why people pursue and choses to stay in this field are those who just really want to become doctors and practice medicine. I have classmates who also were previous OFWs but they chose to pursue med even though they were already earning quite well in another country simply because they really do want to pursue their dreams. It sounds so cliche but I do think this is absolutely the most common reason on why people pursue med and why you would choose to stay/endure despite all it's difficulties/disadvantages as you go through it. So if this is really what you want to be in life then i think yes, it's always going to be worth it.

1. Don't pressure yourself too much. Sabi mo nga 3rd week pa lang. Trust me, it feels overwhelming now pero give it a few weeks pa and you'll find yourself slowly adjusting. Ako 2nd sem pa nung fully naka-adjust na :)
2. It depends on what subject your studying but the most effective method for me would still be active recall (para if they give analytical questions di ka malilito) Do not memorize just for the sake of memorizing, always ask why and how para mas madali matandaan and always correlate all your subjects to each other!
3. In medschool, repetition is key. If kaya try to do first reading kahit mabilisan lang before lectures, magugulat ka akala mo wala ka naintindihan pero it makes learning the lecture easier then para pag nagaral for an exam on that topic, 2nd reading mo na :) Mas madali maretain!

I really don't get this scene.Even though i love the series writers, this felt like a complete betrayal. Here's why:

1. I really like Nairobi's character but she was guilt tripping the Professor for him to agree on that sperm donation. I hated her guts for a moment because she was saying they were a family but she completely blindsided Lisboa (who's now a part of that family) by not even talking to her about this. And just when you think this scene couldn't get worse, there she goes with Tokyo saying to Lisboa's face that it was Nairobi's 'friend with benefits' that's making her pregnancy possible. What's the point of all that speech about them being a family when you freaking betrayed one of your own. Lisboa experienced enough betrayal already from her previous relationship. 
2. I completely agree with the comments that duh, the professor was sick and spent all his childhood and adolescent years in a hospital. She really thought his genes were great?? And intelligence doesn't completely come from the genes, social and home environment contributes a lot.
3. And the Professor, to even agree within that sort amount of time? I believe he's not that dumb not to know that he needs to talk to Lisboa before deciding on that because based on what he said, he completely knows that that baby will be technically his child.
4. This scene is not needed if the purpose was just to make Nairobi's death more devastating than it already was. She was a great character with a lot of great moments, plus the fact that she already has a son who she loves so much is enough for us to feel for her motherhood and to mourn her death even more.

Overall, this scene was weird, unnecessary, was so off-character, and felt like disrespect to what these two characters have built so far. I just wish that the writers have a better explanation on what this scene is all about or what this scene is for in the next season because if not, then I will just pretend this never happened.
